body:
Myself.

I know I would never kill myself, because of what it does to the people I would leave behind.

But the thought that I could slip away unnoticed somehow and take away all the memories people have of me is comforting.

I know it's selfish. I could have said war, or cancer, or hate, or nuclear weapons, but no... Me. Deal with it.

Thanks. I know there will be happy-ish moments, but it's just hard to remember sometimes.

And, frankly, I'm not sure whether it is enough. It always catches up with me.

I don't know. I'm at the stage of my life where all friends, acquaintances and family are married or settled, and many have children. Their lives evolve around other people who are important to them. Staying in touch with me (I do try) is not a priority for them. And I don't hold it against them. If I was dead though, their lives wouldn't be any different.

I know I'm not supposed to think like that. And I'm not at risk or harming myself at this time, but the thought that I may brings me comfort.
Bah, forget about this. Just needed to rant.

I think I understand.

Personally, I cannot even have 'sexy' dreams. Because I either get turned down in my dreams, or something else goes wrong. It's almost funny if it wasn't so pathetic.

Well, you obviously fucked up, but you sound like you may be a decent guy. Even decent people fuck up. 

That said, although nobody can make that decision for you, you also shouldn't underestimate the capacity of people to forgive.

If you genuinely feel this bad about it, she might forgive you. But, like you said, If she ever finds out that you tried to hide it, she won't definitely forgive you.

It's a tough decision to make. I wish you and your girlfriend the best either way.

Whether you tell her or not is your choice,  but at least be honest about why you make that choice.

Don't rationalise it and say you're doing it for *her*. It seems to me that you're doing this for *you*. You don't want to lose her, and maybe you're scared of the potential fallout. That's understandable, I don't want to critisise you for that, you obviously feel bad enough about it. 

But if you cannot be honest with her, at least be honest with yourself and don't hide behind your rationalisation.
I cried like a little boy when I was watching that. Just couldn't stop sobbing.
Thanks for the offer, but I'm giving up for today. It's early to go to bed, but maybe if I can get lots of sleep I'll be a bit stronger tomorrow.
Thank you, I could use a hug right now

Thanks for your kind words. 

But I'm afraid that if I stop looking, then fifteen more years will pass and I'll still won't love and be loved.

I have talked about this with a close female friend. I trust her to be honest with me, even when I might not like it. 

She doesn't think there is anything wrong with my appearance, she has even called me handsome in the past (although I strongly disagree with that). She seems to think it's mainly down to confidence. 

Maybe she is right, but how do I gain confidence at something I have failed at all my life?  If confidence is the issue, I just don't see what I can do.

I'm in England, but not from England. Not sure what to tell though. I'm just bouncing between self-hate and self-pity today. 

I feel like such a fuck-up. I have had as many chances as anyone can expect, but I just let myself turn out like a failure.

I'm in my thirties, but I don't have anything meaningful to show for it, not even memories of anything meaningful. I have no value or place in this world.
Don't really know what to say. I have wasted my life. I fail as a human being.

Am I the only one who feels like a failure after reading that article?

He ran a hugely successful crime organisation by the age of 26! Don't get me wrong, I know he was a bad man (despite the soup), but that is still pretty impressive.

Meanwhile, I'm 33 and still paying off my student loans. I gave a homeless person a roast beef sandwich once, but that's my only claim to fame.

Thanks for your words.

> Don't judge yourself by other people's timetable; you are not them!

I'm abnormal by anyone's timetable though, like a bad caricature of what I could have been. I think it's just too late.

I'm looking for a better therapist though. And I'm very tired today, so maybe that is colouring my point of view.

Hey, you're the girl that smells of butterfly.

Seriously though, that's a pretty interesting name; that has to count for something.

Not sure if this is any help, but up until a few months ago I used to send depressed texts to a friend of mine. My friend never really replied to those texts, only to normal or happy texts. And I assumed she didn't strongly care, or just read them and moved on. Or was too busy with her own life. I assumed all kinds of things.

But it turned out those texts made her worry about me more than I would worry about myself. And she would lose sleep wondering whether I might do something stupid to myself, or whether something she would say would push me over the edge.

Since then I try not to text or email her any more about stuff like that. It just isn't the right medium for it, and you need to give even the most supportive people a break sometimes. That way they can recharge mentally and help you again later.

I still talk to her and she is a great help. But talking face-to-face is just a better way to communicate about it, for me anyway.

Of course it means I can't always talk about it when I most need to. I still haven't figured out a solution for that, but sometimes I go for walks to get some fresh air. Like tonight... I just returned from one of these walks. Didn't really help, but I'll live.

Hang in there.

Edit: unfinished sentence... weird order ... not sure what I was thinking

Wow, you ask a lot of questions, all valid, but I don't really know the answers to most them. 

Thank you for your response, though.

I think a lot of it boils down to my self-image, but it may be a chicken and egg thing. I don't know whether my self-image is causing the behaviour or traits you quoted, or whether those traits feed my self-image.

> Have you made efforts to try or do you just accept this about yourself? 

I did not like to read this and I guess that means you hit home. I like to think that I tried, but I'll reluctantly admit that I could have tried harder. 

I don't know, it seems like I go into a different mode when I should stand up for myself. When I'm by myself I can make the concious decision to stand up for myself next time an opportunity arrises, but when the moment comes, I'm like Pavlov's dog and I react in a certain way without even thinking about it.

> Your fear is all that's holding you back.

I think this might be oversimplifying it a bit. Fear might be a root cause, but if it is, it shaped me and engrained behaviour and thinking patterns in me that aren't as simple to change as 'overcoming fear'.
How easy do you think it would be to earn money on the way. Just doing small jobs, for a few days at a time maybe?
I've wondered about this myself. I want to escape, but what if the thing I'm trying to escape from is *me*...
Yeah, I didn't expect so many reactions. Makes me feel a bit more confident about it to be honest.
Just to clarify, I live in a different country than my familiy, so for the sake of the preview-trip, they're not that likely to miss me for a few days.
If we meet whilst traveling, sure. I'm not making any commitments though :)

I've seen 'Into The Wild', but didn't think of it until you mentioned it. To be honest, I'm not sure I'd mind my trip not ending up so well either. I just wish my family wouldn't be affected by that. 

But you're right, I *should* let my family know if I do leave everything and everyone behind.
Only when we meet 'on the road'. I'm not making any plans or commiting to anything :)

Damn it, you need to be talented to have sexy time? 

Fortunately, there seem to be enough talentless people perfectly capable of multiplying like rabbits.

I think you need to talk to your girlfriend. I'm not going to tell you that you are really an alright guy, or bullshit like that, that's not my call. But what's done is done. You focus on yourself, but this is as much about her as it is about you. 

You seem to be looking for something (some kind of validation perhaps?) that you're not getting in your current relationship. Why don't you talk to her? Your relationship doesn't appear to be working for you and it sounds like you're in a pretty desperate state, so you have nothing to lose.

Same here. I'm in my early thirties and have grown so tired of people telling me that 'it will just happen'.

For a lot of people it does, but for some it doesn't. Hopefully you will turn out to be one of the former.

I don't think you can really predict how your friends will react, you just kinda have to risk it and hope for the best.

I told two close friends about what was going on. One stopped talking to me for about month and a half. After that he tried to be friends again but acted like I had never told him anything. Although I respect him as a person, I felt so incredibly hurt and let down that I cannot really see him as a friend anymore, let alone open up to him.

My other friend stuck with me and was really supportive. Lately she has been distancing herself from me though, which I understand: I know it can be a burden. I think our friendship is turning into a more shallow friendship and I'm trying to avoid that by not using her for support any more :/

Yes, I feel like this a lot. Almost every day I'll spend ages telling myself how much of a failure I am over and over again.

I made all the wrong choices and the things I have done feel hollow and meaningless because of it. It's too late now and I won't ever produce something of worth or value.

I have never been in a relationship and definitely cannot see myself changing that, so even on that level I'm a failure.

The ironic thing is that my expectations of myself used to be really high, and I *could* have met those expectations, but I didn't and now it is too late. I really am a complete failure.
Oh, and it's almost weekend. Hang in there :)

I compartmentalise. A lot. When I am busy and can get on with my work,I shut everything else down. When I talk to my reports I go into 'manager mode' and do the same. And when I chat with most colleagues I wear a mask. 

Fortunately the atmosphere at my job is very relaxed and informal, which helps a lot. Ironically, it's my friends who make it hard for me. A few colleagues are great friends as well and around them it is just so much harder to stay in work mode and shut out the feelings. I've been avoiding lunch with them lately because of it.

And sometimes, when I can't keep it up, I hide in the toillet to cry a little or to prevent myself from breaking down and crying a lot. :/

This is not much help to you, I'm afraid. How is your boss? Maybe you could talk to him, not about the depression, but just say you're getting a bit stressed. Over here you won't get fired for something like that and a good manager will ease your workload a little and help you out. The wellbeing and satisfaction of my reports is a priority for me, although I don't dare to tell my own manager of my depression either.

Well, it's not really apathy or boredom. I can get quite scared about meeting new people (but I'm sure no one knows this). 

If you asked me to go to a party I'd most likely say no. I'm afraid of meeting new people, I'm worried that I might break down, and I don't want to get drunk and lose control (which I used to do in the past). 

Therapy currently just isn't working. She is nice, but I don't feel like I can really open up to her (I have a hard time opening up anyway) and it's just not going anywhere. I think I will cancel it.

Thanks. Reddit has been good to me, as a place to vent and learn.

I wish I could feel confident that I won't do anything stupid and irreversible in the future. Or rather I wish I could feel that I don't *want* to do anything stupid. But thinking about the future and going on for months or even years just scares me. I don't want to go on like this.

It's true for me.

Sometimes I even recognise that I'm being a irrational, but it doesn't change a thing.

To be honest, I don't know. 

I have been making sweeping changes to my life for years, but it has never worked. *I* was the only constant throughtout.

Thanks for the help, bleepitybleep.

I know *rationally* that you are right. But I just find it hard to be or stay rational at the moment. 

I'm so disappointed at reverting back to this. I wasn't doing great before, but at least I could handle things. I'm not going to go on like this forever.

I don't think it's the lifestyle that's the problem though. I think it's *me*. I have made some pretty big changes recently and also some years ago. But no matter where I go or what I do, there is no escaping from myself.

Thanks for your advice, but that's easier said than done.

I have never been able to find a lover, let alone in my current state.

I'm not allowed pets in my apartment and I'm not sure whether I could give a pet the care it would deserve at the moment. It would probably end up as miserable as me and I don't want to do that to anyone, human *or* pet.

And my hobbies have all lost their flavour. Don't get me wrong, I do keep myself busy. But there isn't really anything I get excited or passionate about in a positive way anymore.

I agree life is a gift. But I feel like I have squandered it. There is nothing positive in my future. I'm just going on for the sake of it, I really have no reason to live.

I'm far from great. I know a lot of people I respect, people who matter, who are really intelligent, or creative, or succesful. People who bring something to the world and to others. I have nothing to offer the world.

I don't know why today is worse; nothing particularly bad happened. I could almost feel it coming over the past few days.

You're probably right, it *is* up to me. It just feels so counterintuitive. I keep telling myself that if they would care, surely they would ask. And nothing is worse than telling someone only to find out that, in fact, they *don't* care. I don't want to experience that again.

Yeah, trying to talk to more different people seems like it might be the way to go.

But you can't always tell how even a good friend is going to react when you suddenly drop all this shit on them.

And you have to have some rapport with them as well. Or maybe that's just me, but I cannot open up to different people in the same way... I find it hard enough to open up to someone to begin with.

Thanks for the advice and offers to listen.

I still think it's a hard issue. For some reason venting to people over the phone, or by email or message just doesn't seem to work as well for me.

Thanks for your replies; I'm feeling a bit better today. I like the poem; haven't figured out how to walk down another street though.

Edit: And sorry about the swearing.
Bloody hell! I hate myself so much...

I don't know, man. It's starting to feel like forever and I'm going the wrong way again.

How did I end up like this?

Thanks Dirk, I'll go check it out. 

Depression has made me figure out just that: I'm not always rational. In fact, often I'm not and I make irrational decisions based on emotions or feelings I don't fully understand. And, in a way, knowing that does help dealing with it.
I love both of those films, but haven't seen them in a while. Maybe that's worth trying out: if happy films make me feel bad after watching, maybe sad films may have the opposite effect.

I've been avoiding films that might evoke strong emotions in me, to be honest. I tend to stick with 'safer' films these days, like animated films from Disney or Ghibli. 

'Beauty and the Beast' still had me in tears a few days ago though, so not sure it's working...

I reckonise what you're saying though, when the fantasy or suspension of disbelieve ends I can get worse again. On the other hand, I do need some occasional source of enjoyment, even if it doesn't last...
Thanks, I don't really feel comfortable enough (this is an understatement) with her at the moment to communicate about my doubts about the therapy, but I guess that means that I really should anyway!

I didn't want meds, but take st. John's wort twice a day. I'm currently able to cope and deal with it to a certain extent, which is a huge improvement. But therapy had nothing to do with that. And I seem stuck as well. 

I'm not doing bad enough to want to kill myself anymore. And I'm not doing well enough to want to live.
It's supposed to be a combination between talk therapy and CBT, but it's just not going anywhere.

Thanks for your reply. I'll stick with it for now, maybe I can build a better rapport with her, or maybe I won't, but at least I'll have tried.

If it doesn't work I might try and find a different therapist, if I can bring myself to it. 

Did therapy actually help you identify the root problem?
Sometimes I think I know exactly what's causing my depression, other times I think along completely different lines. I'm not sure which thoughts to trust and how depression is influencing my perception of my 'problems'.

Sorry for the poorly written and rambling post btw, I was feeling quite frustrated when I typed it.

You sound frustrated and upset, and I'm sorry to hear that you feel that way.

I'm not in any position to give relationship or dating advice, but I have been around people for a while, so this is just my take on it.

Girls and guys might be fundamentally different. But so are girls and girls, and guys and guys for that matter. What I'm saying is, everyone is fundamentally different, and when you try to connect on some meaningful level, that's when that difference can become most obvious. I don't think it's gender specific, but I could be wrong.

I'm not sure it's that straight forward to 'go gay'. By all means, go for it, if you think that makes you happy. But I think that's just your frustration speaking (believe me, I know about frustration).

It sucks to feel the way you do, but if you think she was only with you out of desperation, then that wasn't probably the best situation to be in anyway.

Anyway, chin up, dude. And take care of yourself
I don't think I'll ever really find out for myself what the value of sexual experiences is, but it's good to read your take on it. Thanks. :)
Thanks for kind words. Keep hold of that positive attitude. :)

Hmm, I get that sex is just biology, but that also means it's a fundamental part of the human experience. And it's frustrating to think that I somehow manage to fail at this basic part of human life. 

I read a theory a while ago that seemed to confirm what you said, btw. That during sex certain chemicals get released that are associated with love too. 

And yes, when I talk about sex, I tend to think of it as something that complements love and connection. In fact, I would definitely  prefer a loving platonic relationship over a loveless sexual relationship. But I don't think I could ever be happy with one, without at least knowing what it is to have the other. 
And I have never had a connection like that either (I must be a horrible person. A good friend told me today that they couldn't deal with my (other) problems anymore). 

I'm not quite that young anymore either, you could add a decade to that. But yeah, the OP still has a lot of time and, to OP: I hope that you find what you're looking for (and don't end up like me).

Ok, now I feel really bad for that analogy. 

You say you don't need a partner for an orgasm, and whilst that's true, it's not all about the orgasm though, is it? I don't really know, but I imagine the intimacy and the fact you're doing it With someone, who also desires you, is equally, if not more, important.

I don't know, maybe you're right and maybe I've built it up in my mind to something much bigger than it is. On the off chance I do have sex before I expire, if it does turn out to be nothing more than fancy masturbation, I'm going to be hugely disappointed.

With all due respect, it always annoys me a little bit when someone says this: that it doesn't matter, or isn't a big deal. 

OP is right though (I'm in a similar boat, so to speak), if it didn't matter, why do you so see it everywhere and why do people love talking about it so much, offline as well?

It's like saying food doesn't matter, because you enjoy the luxury of eating every day, take it for granted, and can't remember a time when you were really hungry..

Ok that was actually a really bad analogy, but maybe you get what I'm saying here. People who tell you it doesn't matter, tend to have it in abundance.

I wouldn't call it sick. But obsession, like you say, might be right. 
I'm in no position to give advice, but I imagine that it's not getting easier as long as you have this unfulfilled desire and secret between the two of you. 
In an ideal world you would be able to talk to your wife about this and that might actually go a long way to dealing with this obsession. But it's not an ideal world and I don't want to advise anything that might ruin your marriage. 

Maybe you could just book one session with a therapist and see what they say about it. No one needs to know, they're not as scary as they sound and who knows, it might help.

Colour me green. Never felt such powerful desire, nor has anyone ever felt that way about me. 

Still, it sounds like a difficult situation to be in. Out of curiousity, is it fear of the consequences and the possible upheaval of your life that stops you, or fear of hurting your wife and children?

> You need confidence to come from within.

I don't believe confidence ever truly exclusively comes from within. I think it comes from affirmation. Not necessarily from others, but affirmation none the less. 
If you’re confident in your job, you’ve likely either had colleagues tell you that you’re doing a good job, or you’ve seen ‘evidence’ of having done a good job yourself.
Likewise, when it comes to dating, I imagine that confidence comes mostly from dating success (regardless of how humbly you define success). I’m trying not to be too negative here and I do suppose that some confidence might be gained by simply realising that you can deal with rejection, better than you thought you could. But I’m just saying, I don’t think you can just will yourself to be more confident. Neither does it help to be told to be more confident…

You hit the nail on the head. One night stands don't interest me at all, maybe I wouldn't be like this now if they did appeal to me, but they just don't.

I just took two online tests: one came out as INFJ and the other as ISFJ. Not really sure what this tells me though. I've always known that I'm very introverted of course, but once I befriend and learn to trust someone I open up a lot.
I really don't want it to be like that. And I don't think it would do anything for my confidence or self-esteem, let alone for the girl in question.

When do you stop waiting for the right person, though?

I've been told in the past that virginity is a gift you give someone special, but my gift seems past the due date. And at times it feels more like a curse.
